title: A scribe with a stroke jig, a tray, a running list of the last three pages, and the odd forms of the part he copies
method:
ONE PROCEDURE, written as a scribe's habits, fitted on the 192 public practice pages only. The 34 pages the practice evaluation scores were never fitted on; the hidden held-out pages were never read.

THE PEN. A jig of stroke transitions: given the two strokes before, whether the line is the opening of a paragraph, whether the word closes the line, and which of the two Currier languages the page is in, the jig gives the odds of the next stroke. Eleven levels of backoff, from the full setting down to the bare language, blended by how often each setting was seen. A word is written stroke by stroke until the jig brings the word to its end.

THE PAGE. A page is stocked before it is written: half a packet of slips belonging to the quire of twelve pages it sits in, kept apart for each language of the quire; a quarter out of the chest kept for this part of the book in this hand from first to last; the rest drawn fresh from the same working stock.

WHERE A WORD COMES FROM, for each word in turn:
 -- 20 times in a hundred, a slip from the tray of the last ten words, and not that slip itself but an altered one: one stroke changed, a stroke that fits before and after it, drawn by the same jig, never the stroke already there.
 -- 18 times, a word he has already written on this page.
 -- 16 times, a word he wrote in the last three pages and has not let go of: a running subject is written with the same words while it lasts, and the list of them runs off page by page.
 -- 14 times, a word out of the page's own little set, or out of the quire's, or out of the forms he keeps to for a whole part of the book in one language.
 -- 2 times, a slip out of the page's stock.
 -- the rest, written out by the jig; and of those, about a fifth are taken from the forms the part he copies holds once or twice, each taken up once and no more, so that a form standing once in the old book stands once in his.
Of the words he takes up rather than writes out, he spells each his own way -- at a stroke the pen goes where it is used to going -- and keeps to that way through the quire.

THE LINE. A line is written to the margin: the width is drawn from the fitted distribution of line widths, words are laid down while they fit, and where the room left is small he tries up to three times for a shorter word. The word that stands at the line's end gets the closing stroke of his line-end habit: the last stroke is drawn again, weighted by how often a stroke that follows there closes a line in this language.

THE PARAGRAPH. The opening line of a paragraph is written with the paragraph setting of the jig on, which is what carries the initial strokes there.

RESULT ON THE PRACTICE EVALUATION: 18 of the 22 established facts. It fails four: F-001, F-006, F-013 and F-020.

WHAT THIS VERSION WAS BUILT FOR, and what it got. The previous procedure of mine (R-034, 17 of 22 on the hidden pages) missed F-011, F-014 and F-020. This one reproduces two of them:
 -- F-011, pages close together sharing words: 0.0316 against the across-page shuffle at p = 0.005 (the manuscript 0.074). No setting of the earlier procedure got this fact off the null at all; it needed words that are locally frequent and globally rare, which is what the three-page running list and the once-only forms supply. Taking the quire's stock from the odd forms of the part being copied, rather than from its common ones, is what moved it: the same words have to be shared by the pages of a stretch without being shared by the whole book.
 -- F-014, two word types in three occurring once: 0.680 against the floor of 0.667 (the manuscript 0.711). It comes from the once-only forms being taken up once, and from a plain reluctance to write the same form over and over: a form new to the book is taken as it comes, one written once or twice is taken three times in four, one written often is left for the last.

WHAT IT COSTS, measured. The same three settings that buy those two facts give back others, and the trade-off was followed through six settings of this one procedure:
 -- F-013, the cost of a stroke given the two before: 2.19 against a ceiling of 2.10 (the manuscript 1.94). Every word taken up from a list is a word whose first stroke does not follow from the stroke before it, so the more the scribe takes up the dearer the text reads. Sharpening the pen's say in which slip is lifted -- weighting the choice by the cube of how the jig would take that stroke up here -- brings it from 2.45 down to 2.19 but no further while words are taken up at all.
 -- F-001, line-final m in Currier B: 9.0 against the floor of 10. The line-end stroke is the only thing that holds it and it is diluted by every word taken up whole.
 -- F-007, near-copies in the last ten words, is held by the altered tray slip and passes at 0.193; but the same dial that raises it pushes F-021, one-edit repetition from the line above, out of its band: at a tray rate of 0.22 the copy rate is 0.219 and F-021 goes to 0.052, outside the band 0.012-0.045. The two facts are held by one dial and pull apart.
 -- F-006, longer words at line starts: 4.98, p = 0.55. The margin mechanism leaves this fact weak in every setting tried.
 -- F-020, pages of one Currier language sharing words: -0.006, at the label-shuffled null and under the label-rotated one. The quire packet is kept apart by language and the chest is kept by language, and it still does not clear the null. This is the one fact that no setting of any procedure in this swarm has taken, and it is where this attempt stands too.

CONTROLS. Six settings of the same procedure, all on the same seed, all on the practice evaluation. With the running list off, F-011 falls from 0.032 to -0.006. With the quire stock taken from the common forms of the part being copied instead of the odd ones, F-011 sits at -0.023. With the once-only forms taken up as often as they come, F-014 reaches 0.786, F-013 goes to 2.24 and F-016 falls to 0.16. With the pen's say in which slip is lifted sharpened from flat to the cube of the jig's odds, F-013 comes down from 2.45 to 2.13. With the tray rate at 0.18 instead of 0.20, F-001 stands at 12.0 and F-007 at 0.186; at 0.22, F-007 stands at 0.219 and F-001 at 6.2. Nothing here is fitted to a target pattern and no rule names one; the numbers are the run's.

GUARDS. 4,487 ordinary lines and 738 paragraph-opening lines, exactly the manuscript's counts; 40,355 tokens; 0 four-word runs of the manuscript; 0 uncertainty markers.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW: that the manuscript is or is not a language, or meaningless. It shows that one page-level fact (F-011) and one vocabulary-level fact (F-014) can be had by a procedure with a locally-held, globally-rare stock, and that holding them costs the stroke-level facts (F-013, F-001) in the same procedure -- which is what one would expect if the manuscript's stroke-level structure and its page-level structure have different causes.
